name: Caer Darrow
summary: Phantoms haunt Caer Darrow above Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. House Barov once ruled from its keep, now sold to Kel'Thuzad and remade as Scholomance.

sections.title: A Legacy of War and Betrayal
sections.body: Caer Darrow guarded Lordaeron and held an ancient elven runestone long before the Scourge. During the Second War, the Horde sacked the fortress and broke the stone apart for Gul'dan's Altars of Storms. Lord Uther the Lightbringer sailed to aid the survivors, but Alterac privateers ambushed his fleet. Their treachery exposed Alterac's betrayal to the Alliance.

sections.title: The Fall of House Barov
sections.body:
After the Second War, Caer Darrow rose again as the Barov family's grand estate. Their vast land deeds reached across Brill, Tarren Mill, and Southshore. When age threatened their wealth and mortality, the Barovs bargained with Kel'Thuzad. The Cult of the Damned took root beneath the fortress and founded Scholomance.

Before the Third War swept across Lordaeron, a preliminary plague struck the island's servants and townsfolk. They perished, doomed to haunt the ruined keep as lingering echoes.

faq.answer: Caer Darrow rises as an island fortress in Darrowmere Lake, within the Western Plaguelands. Once the ancestral manor of the wealthy Barov family, it is now a ruin above Scholomance's catacombs, a necromantic academy.

faq.q: Why is the town abandoned and ruined?
faq.answer: Caer Darrow was abandoned after the Barov family bargained with Kel'Thuzad and gave their estate to the Cult of the Damned in exchange for immortality. The cult loosed a fatal plague upon the settlement before Lordaeron's wider invasion began.

faq.q: Why can't I see the ghosts in the town?
faq.answer: The murdered inhabitants of Caer Darrow linger as restless spirits, caught in their final moments. Ordinary eyes cannot see them without special magical sight, such as the Spectral Essence provided by the spirits of Eva and Lucien Sarkhoff.

faq.q: What was the runestone that used to be here?
faq.answer: During the Second War, Caer Darrow held an ancient high elven runestone. The Horde raided the island and chiseled the sacred stone into pieces. Gul'dan used them to build the Altars of Storms and channel magic into ogre mages.

Scholomance lies beneath the keep as the Cult of the Damned's headquarters and training academy. Led by Darkmaster Gandling, its necromancers and acolytes study the dark arts and experiment on the dead.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Caer Darrow recalls two betrayals. Alterac privateers ambushed Lord Uther the Lightbringer's fleet during the Second War, exposing King Perenolde's treason. Later, House Barov sold its ancestral home to Kel'Thuzad.
As a human, you can recognize Caer Darrow as the former seat of House Barov, once among Lordaeron's wealthiest noble families. Their greed led them to make pacts with the Cult of the Damned.
